newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees liberalized sugar market by mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees liberalized sugar market by mid-1998.

text.p: The Brazilian government hopes to completely liberate the sugar market, including exports, by mid-1998, a senior commodities official said.

Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, told reporters the aim was to liberate the market at the time prices for hydrous alcohol are freed up in May 1998.
"We are working towards liberating the alcohol and sugar sector from the moment it becomes viable to free up hydrous alcohol prices in May 1998," he said.
Prices of anhydrous alcohol, which is mixed in Brazil with gasoline at a proportion of 22 percent, will be liberalized this May.
Assis noted that four million vehicles still ran on hydrous alcohol in Brazil and that the government was committed to "ensuring supply" for those cars.

"The idea is to liberate the whole sector in May 1998 but we have to resolve the problem of hydrous alcohol first, that is, we have until May 1998, or in fact the end of this year, to resolve the problem," Assis said.
Liberalization would mean the end of export quotas.

Both hydrous and anhydrous alcohol prices had been due to be liberated at the beginning of the year but under pressure from distillers for more time to adapt to the free market, the government put its plans on hold.
Among options being discussed to replace federal subsidies are ecological taxes on other fuels.
